title: Kippers on toast with sharp blackberry relish

grandparents_cupboard.reason: Kippers, blackberries, shallot, cider vinegar, bread and butter are all traditional kitchen staples with nothing factory-made.

supermarket.reason: Kippers, watercress and September blackberries are everyday Tesco lines at ordinary prices.

basic_kitchen.reason: It needs only a frying pan, a bowl and a toaster, and poaching kippers in boiling water is beginner-level.

works.reason: Jugging four kipper fillets for 4 minutes and serving them on buttered toast with a sharp berry relish gives a sound breakfast for four.

honest_times.reason: Halving 200g of berries, chopping a shallot and dill, and toasting four slices fits comfortably in 12 minutes, and the 4-minute simmer matches the 5 cook minutes.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed item, including the dill and lemon, appears in the steps, and the names match their ids.

seasonal_feel.reason: Early September is peak blackberry time, and the 200g relish is a substantial sharp foil to the oily kipper in the way gooseberry goes with mackerel, not a scattered garnish.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are short, plain British English that a neighbour could follow.

hearty_healthy.reason: Oily fish on wholemeal toast with watercress and fruit makes a proper, nourishing breakfast.
